product_offering.core_offering: Hebbia provides an AI reasoning platform called Matrix that enables financial professionals to analyze millions of documents, reason over unlimited context, and automate end-to-end financial workflows such as investment memos, board decks, and diligence summaries. The platform integrates private documents, public filings, and third-party financial data providers into a unified environment for institutional investors, investment banks, advisory firms, and corporate finance teams.
product_offering.differentiator: Purpose-built AI for finance with unmatched scale (30T AUM, 200K+ prompts/day, 1.5B pages processed). Integrates private documents, public filings, and leading financial data providers (FactSet, PitchBook, S&P Capital IQ, Guidepoint, Third Bridge) in one platform. Workflow automation for end-to-end financial processes.
product_offering.functional_benefit: 1) Reasoning over limitless context across millions of documents; 2) Automated workflows for investment memos, board decks, diligence summaries; 3) Connect private documents, public filings, and financial data providers; 4) Enterprise collaboration for institutional knowledge sharing; 5) Identify red flags and opportunities from earnings calls, filings, expert calls.
product_offering.problem_solved: Financial professionals struggle with: 1) Manually reviewing millions of documents; 2) Fragmented data across multiple sources; 3) Slow research and analysis processes; 4) Inability to scale insights across organizations; 5) Difficulty reasoning across complex financial datasets without hallucination or keyword-matching limitations.
quantifiable_outcome: 10,000+ slides automated per day via FlashDocs
Processing of 1,256+ document analyses (example in Airlines Earnings Calls)
product_offering.product_overview: Hebbia is an AI platform for finance offering a unified product called Matrix, which provides institutional intelligence through AI-powered document analysis, financial data integration, and automated workflows. The platform supports four key solution areas: Institutional Investing, Investment Banking, Professional Services, and Corporate Finance & Strategy. Through the acquisition of FlashDocs, Hebbia expanded into generative AI content creation, specifically automated slide deck generation. The platform integrates with multiple data providers (FactSet, PitchBook, S&P Capital IQ, Guidepoint, Third Bridge) and document management systems to enable end-to-end financial workflows.

profiles.name: George Sivulka
profiles.overview: CEO and Founder of Hebbia, who has developed techniques enabling AI to answer questions about large datasets without merely regurgitating information or fabricating responses.
profiles.profile_commentary: George Sivulka founded Hebbia in 2020 and serves as CEO. He has driven the development of Hebbia's AI reasoning platform that addresses the limitations of traditional retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) by analyzing actual user intent rather than keyword matches. Under his leadership, Hebbia has grown to serve major financial institutions including KKR and Morgan Stanley, raised $130 million from Andreessen Horowitz at a $700 million valuation in late 2024, and acquired FlashDocs in mid-2025 to expand into content generation.

profiles.overview: Technical co-founder of FlashDocs, a generative AI slide deck creation company founded in 2024, which was acquired by Hebbia in 2025.

Following Hebbia's acquisition of FlashDocs in June 2025, Bruun joined Hebbia where the FlashDocs team leads API business and artifact generation.

recent_move.description: Raised $130 million led by Andreessen Horowitz at a $700 million post-money valuation, providing multi-year capital to scale the Matrix platform and finance vertical.

Acquired FlashDocs, a generative AI slide deck creation company automating 10,000+ slides per day, expanding Hebbia from information retrieval into content generation and establishing an API/artifact business.
Partnered with FactSet to integrate its financial data and analytics directly into the Hebbia platform for AI-driven research.
Joined PitchBook's 2025 LLM partner cohort (alongside Anthropic, Perplexity, Rogo), embedding PitchBook's private capital market data into Hebbia workflows.
Integrated with Microsoft Azure AI Foundry, leveraging hyperscaler AI infrastructure for enhanced scale and credibility with enterprise procurement.
Formed a strategic partnership with Third Bridge to embed expert call research inside the Hebbia platform, broadening primary-research workflow coverage.

expansion_highlight.description: Hebbia added FactSet (2025-09), PitchBook (2025-08), Microsoft Azure AI Foundry (2025-08), and Third Bridge (2025-07) as core integration partners, systematically positioning Matrix as the orchestration layer between proprietary data providers and AI infrastructure. The cadence suggests a deliberate "land and expand" ecosystem strategy.

The FlashDocs acquisition (2025-06) marks Hebbia's first disclosed M&A and signals a willingness to use capital to enter adjacent product surfaces (generative content/API/artifact generation). With $130M of fresh capital and a16z backing, additional tuck-in acquisitions in AI-native workflow tooling are plausible.

The FlashDocs team was tasked to lead API business and artifact generation at Hebbia, opening a new product surface (programmatic access, embedded AI artifacts) that extends the business beyond internal-seat SaaS into developer/platform monetization.

Hebbia's named customer list extends beyond buy-side and investment banking into insurance (MetLife), legal services (Latham & Watkins), and corporate strategy, indicating vertical expansion beyond pure institutional investing into adjacent professional knowledge work.

The $130M round from a16z at a $700M valuation (2024-12) is a significant capital signal relative to a 2020 founding, providing multi-year runway and the option value to fund aggressive go-to-market, M&A, and product expansion without near-term fundraising pressure.

Observed contracts include both per-seat ($800-$1,000/user/month) and annual platform-fee (e.g., SwipeCo) structures, and the new API business opens programmatic/usage-based monetization, suggesting a multi-modal pricing strategy rather than seat-only SaaS.
